base.description: The chassis as Juniper ships MX10008-BASE. One routing and control board with a cover over the second slot. Three power supplies with a cover over each of the other three, fans, and a cover in each of the eight line-card slots. Line cards are ordered separately.
base.source: vendor - Juniper publishes this as an orderable bundle. The hardware guide's 'MX10008 Components and Configurations' table (MX10008-BASE) lists one RCB with one Routing Control Board cover, three power supplies with three power supply covers, and eight line card covers, over the note that line cards and the cable management system are not part of the base configuration. The table gives no part number for the RCB or power supply covers; JNP10K-RE-BLNK and JNP10K-PWR-BLNK, named for the same cages in the MX10004 guide, are carried over. This base draws exactly that: one board in RCB slot 0 and its cover in slot 1, three supplies and a cover in each of the other three supply slots, and a cover in each of the eight line-card slots. The five switch fabric boards and their cover sit inside the chassis, not visible from outside, and no bay for them is drawn.

datasheet.title: Juniper MX10000 Modular 5G Universal Routing Platforms datasheet (MX10008/MX10016)

description: Juniper MX10008 - the 13RU, eight-slot MX10000 chassis. Two JNP10K-RE1 Routing and Control Boards stack under the badge strip beside the status lamp panel; eight full-width line-card slots (FPC 0-7) fill the front in two banks of four. The rear is a six-high PSU stack beside two tall fan trays covering the Switch Interface Boards.

gaps.wanted: a photograph of a real RCB's model label. The board in this chassis's own photographs carries four SFP cages numbered 0-3 and no BITS, ToD, RESET or Online/Offline hardware, which matches neither Juniper faceplate figure - not Figure 46 (JNP10K-RE1 family, two reserved XGE cages) nor Figure 45 (JNP10K-RE3 family). juniper/jnp10k-re1@2 follows the figure it is named for; the detail is in provenance/which-board-the-photographs-show on that contract. The label does not resolve at the scale of any photograph held here.
a photograph of the rear - only the isometric line drawing g050553 exists, so PSU stack and fan tray geometry are fractional readings and finish is inferred.
the JNP10K-PWR-AC3 (four-feed) and DC faces; only AC2 is modelled.

a flat figure or square-on photograph of the JNP10K-PWR-AC2 face; the guide gives its outer size (Table 55) and isometric drawings, so juniper/jnp10k-pwr-ac2@2 refits the face of version 1 to 91.4 x 88.9 mm by estimate
LC4800/LC4802 faceplates - named with dimensions and power in the guides but with no usable face art in the extraction.

the switch fabric boards (JNP10008-SF, JNP10008-SF2) and their cover (JNP10008-SF-BLNK2) sit inside the chassis behind the fan trays, where no face shows them. Vendor count is five boards and one cover on the base; none is drawn.

attrs.redundancy-note: 1+1 - mx10008 hardware guide, "MX10008 Component Redundancy": one RCB in the base configuration, two in the redundant one; with two fitted one is primary and the other backup, and the backup takes over if the primary or any part of it fails. The RCB consolidates the Routing Engine function with the control plane function in a single unit, so this one form covers both

power.note: datasheet-table - JNP10K-PWR-AC2 5.5 kW each as the MX10004; the guide also lists the AC3 unit (gap). The MX10000 and MX10008/MX10016 datasheets both state typical power consumption 12 kW, fully loaded, naming no ambient or side - carried as power-typical-w. The guide rates every FRU by ambient (Table 47, including the fan trays: JNP10008-FAN 475 W, -FAN2 1207 W, -FAN3 1620 W) and works an example of 14,110 W for eight MX10K-LC2101 in a redundant configuration (2710 W + 11,400 W) - a sample, not carried

rear.note: drawing - g050553 (isometric, fractions only): one six-high stack of JNP10K-PWR supplies at the left, two tall fan trays right. The MX10008 rear has no usable photograph in the intake - see gaps. Each supply bay is 91.4 x 88.9 mm, the JNP10K-PWR-AC2 as the guide's Table 55 gives it (3.6 in. wide, 3.5 in. high; guide page 184), and the six stand one above the next with no gap, as the figure draws them, the earthing terminal's strip below PSU 5. The bays were 84.0 x 93.5 mm, spread over the fan trays' height. The guide's Table 12 gives the fan trays 6.6 in. (16.8 cm, about 167.6 mm) wide and 22.4 in. (56.9 cm) high (guide page 61), and juniper/jnp10008-fan@2, juniper/jnp10008-fan2@2 and juniper/jnp10008-fan3@2 are drawn at that size; juniper/jnp10008-fan@1, juniper/jnp10008-fan2@1 and juniper/jnp10008-fan3@1, 176 x 560 mm from the drawing, are kept for a saved rack that names them. The two fan bays are 167.6 x 569.0 mm, the size of the QFX10008's, and stand against the supply column and against each other, centred in the 574 mm height (y 2.5). 91.4 + 2 x 167.6 mm is 426.6 mm of the 442 mm body, and no figure shows the other 15.4 mm, so it is left empty at the right edge, an estimate

slot-numbering.note: guide - FPC 0-7 top-down (the CLI terminology table maps FPC n, n 0-7, to the slots); the photograph's slot labels are not legible, so top-down follows the family convention
